meta.title: The Tree of IRIX 7
meta.description: A living, interactive map of the IRIX 7 operating system roadmap: one logical computer from 1 to 128 nodes.
intro: IRIX 7 is a clean-room, Rust-native operating system that runs IRIX 6.5 binaries and grows into one logical computer: 1–128 kernel replicas sharing one capability graph.
The Tree is its living roadmap. The roots are the Indy baseline and the first gates, the trunk is the mesh, and the branches are the native compatibility, display, runtime and scale-out tracks.
Nothing here is a date. It is a map of what must be true before the next thing can grow.
meta.note: Grown from docs/project/milestones.md. Statuses sync from the IRIX 7 Roadmap project.

nodes.title: IRIX 7
nodes.subtitle: 1–128 nodes · IP24
nodes.summary: One logical computer built from 1 to 128 kernel replicas, with the native Indy and the IRIX compatibility track at its base.

nodes.title: Toolchain
nodes.summary: The cross-build, Nix shell and CI gate that make the native Indy and every later shim possible.
nodes.demo: CI cross-builds the ROM, kernel and native targets; the toolchain gate is green.
criteria: `-Z build-std` builds `core` and `alloc` for the MIPS targets.
The Nix devshell pins rustc, GCC, binutils and the target specs.
The ROM, kernel and native targets cross-build from a clean checkout.
The x86_64 and PowerPC targets are checked in the same gate.
The release toolchain is reproducible.
nodes.deps: The pinned nightly, Nix, GCC/binutils and the target specs.
nodes.risks: Nightly drift; GCC-backend disk; host-toolchain glue.
nodes.note: Done. The tree keeps it as a root.

nodes.title: Single-node
nodes.summary: One logical computer with no network, quorum or seed: local namespace, CAS, capabilities, actors and devices, plus the native POSIX/IRIX smoke.
nodes.demo: The Indy boots to `BOOT-READY` with no mesh RPCs; the local policy runs natively and from a Wasm guest; the native `std` image exits 0.
criteria: M1 gate on iris: zero mesh RPCs and local namespace, CAS, capability and actor policy.
The `logical` module runs the local policy and ticks three times.
The slot-B Wasm module runs the same policy from a Rust guest.
MCP stays in slot A; the ABI 11 user image boots.
The native `std` image boots with `net=off` and exits 0.
Real-Indy limitation recorded: no physical IP24 attached to the gate.
nodes.deps: M0; the Indy shim; the fixed PROM service table.
nodes.risks: PROM headroom; real-Indy SCC/Seeq/SCSI/REX3 timing; Wasm load time.
nodes.note: Complete on iris; the real-Indy hardware pass is still tracked in #16.

nodes.title: Two-node
nodes.summary: Two independent kernels: signed join, membership epoch, rendezvous homes, remote capabilities, L0 migration and failure fencing.
nodes.demo: Two iris kernels converge on one epoch; a capability routes to its home; an actor migrates both ways; a killed or partitioned peer is fenced and the survivor continues.
criteria: Signed join and epoch convergence on two real kernels.
Rendezvous homes with no central directory.
Remote capability route with one `MOVED` retry.
L0 actor migration both ways at a message boundary.
Failure and partition fencing with a write lease shorter than the failure window.
The epoch store survives member and root restarts.
nodes.deps: M1; the M2 rig; two iris instances.
nodes.risks: Gossip/epoch push; replicated epoch log; linearisable write handover.
nodes.note: Closed on the two-kernel rig; gossip, a replicated epoch log and general migration are follow-ups.

nodes.title: Eight-node
nodes.summary: Eight-node sharded homes, CAS fetch, placement, churn and two-node failure on real kernels.
nodes.demo: Two real kernels pass the first shard slice: epoch 2, the same 32-object table, a remote stat and stale-epoch refusal. Eight kernels boot; convergence is still gated on the transport fix.
criteria: Eight-node join and refresh; sharded homes over the confirmed view.
CAS fetch and placement with no central directory.
Mesh streams, multi-peer transport and larger buffers.
Two-node failure, churn and stale-epoch refusal.
GPU object path and eight-node convergence on real kernels.
Host tests at 1/2/8/128 nodes; real-kernel evidence.
nodes.deps: M2; the shard slice; the M3 rig.
nodes.risks: Eight-node smoltcp receive truncation; multi-peer transport; CAS fetch; churn.
nodes.note: The first shard slice passes on two kernels; eight-node convergence is not claimed.

nodes.title: 128-node
nodes.summary: 128 replicas with at most two normal hops, no global queue or lock, and a simulator that uses the kernel's own mesh policy.
nodes.demo: A 128-node simulator with fault and churn injection, plus x86_64 cloud nodes; hop, RPC, gossip and lease metrics stay bounded.
criteria: 128 replicas; at most two normal forwarding hops.
No global queue, lock, all-to-all gossip or central directory.
Eight-node failure; 64/64 partition; membership churn.
1M OIDs and 10k actors.
Cloud VirtIO; cross-architecture state hashes.
The same `mesh-core`/`mesh-service` policy in the simulator and the kernel.
nodes.deps: M3; x86_64 and cloud shims; the 128-node simulator.
nodes.risks: Scheduler scale; cloud runner capacity; authority and lease scale.
nodes.note: The first x86_64 PVH slice and the PowerPC G3 serial boot are in; cloud and the 128-node gate remain.

nodes.title: IRIX compat
nodes.summary: The native POSIX/relibc layer and the IRIX 6.5 container: the compatibility mandate stays native while the mesh core grows.
nodes.demo: A relibc-linked C probe boots on the native gate; the o32 loader probe runs open/read/write/close/exit; next is the full IRIX container.
criteria: POSIX.1-2024 contract through the clean-room relibc fork.
n32 negative errno, 136-byte `stat`, auxiliary vector and `$28` TCB.
o32 loader/syscall probe; the IRIX 6.5 container is still ahead.
IRIX libc, `rld`, `sproc`, signals and the compatibility corpus.
The native `std` image still boots.
nodes.deps: M1; the native gate; the relibc fork.
nodes.risks: IRIX libc surface; TLS/TCB; o32 container; big-endian.
nodes.note: The o32 probe is not an IRIX 6.5 binary; `rld`/`sproc`/signals are still ahead.

nodes.title: Display
nodes.summary: Newport REX3, damage repair, a native display server and an IRIX-inspired desktop.
nodes.demo: A native window with text and a hardware cursor moves and repairs by damage; the desktop has a launcher and clock.
criteria: Newport REX3 blit, fill, line and text with `rgbmode` and a drained FIFO.
VC2 mode programming and the XMAP9 palette.
Hardware cursor, retained windows and damage-driven repair.
Display lease for a full-screen cell.
A native desktop: launcher, window manager, clock, terminal.
The long-range COSMIC fork stays on the GPU-node path (#194).
nodes.risks: Undocumented VRAM; REX3 FIFO depth; input.
nodes.note: The REX3 driver is verified; the desktop is still a design target.

nodes.title: X11
nodes.summary: Run real IRIX X clients under a clean-room Rust X11 server in display-lease mode.
nodes.demo: `xterm` and `twm` run under X11 on the Indy; the keyboard and mouse work; the server survives an X client crash.
criteria: X11 connection handshake, MSBFirst, setup reply.
Core protocol: windows, GCs, pixmaps, fonts, events, properties, selections.
8-bit PseudoColor and 24-bit TrueColor visuals.
SHAPE, a local MIT-SHM equivalent and XTEST.
Xlib ABI subset sufficient for `xterm`/`twm`.
Display lease integration and a clean-room server.
nodes.risks: Xlib/Motif surface; protocol corner cases; performance.
nodes.note: `x11rb`/`yserver` are the current candidates; the server is not started.

nodes.title: XFS
nodes.summary: Read an IRIX 6.5 XFS v4 disk image: superblock, allocation groups, inodes, extents and the bmap B+tree.
nodes.demo: `ls /mnt/irix` lists an IRIX 6.5 disk image and `cat` reads a file.
criteria: Superblock, AG headers, inode core, extents and the bmap B+tree.
Four directory forms, symlinks and the clean-log check.
Big-endian metadata; no byte swapping on the hot path.
Refuses a dirty log with a clear message.
A test corpus of clean IRIX 6.5 images.
No log replay and no write path in v1.0.
nodes.risks: IRIX v4 specifics (v1 dirs, ACLs); dirty logs; corrupted images.
nodes.note: Research only; `lamxfs`/`xfs-core` are candidates, not adopted.

nodes.title: Runtime & cells
nodes.fullTitle: Runtime, native cells and capability ABI
nodes.summary: The capability engine, namespace/CAS and native cell ABI that make the mesh policy real on every node.
nodes.demo: The local policy runs from a Rust Wasm guest; cap-engine verifies a 1-of-1 capability; CAS/namespace resolves local objects; native cells open files and call servers.
criteria: Capability engine: Ed25519, trust roots, 1-of-1 authority and rights.
Namespace tree over canonical directory objects; CAS put/pin.
Native cell loader, rights, IPC/ports and a Unix-shaped libc.
Wasm policy host and deterministic fuel metering.
Threshold roots and revocation remain Phase 8.
nodes.risks: Capability/namespace impedance; Wasm stack; authority scale.
nodes.note: The shared crates are merged; the resident core and full authority remain.

nodes.title: Real Indy
nodes.summary: The native Indy daily driver and the v1.0 release gate: the old machine, the new logical computer and the compatibility track in one image.
nodes.demo: A real Indy cold-boots from the ROM, joins the mesh, runs the native compatibility track and updates with rollback.
criteria: Cold boot on the supported real Indys.
M1–M4 gates pass on the supported matrix; recorded limitations are closed.
Native POSIX/IRIX, display/X11/XFS and native cells have a v1.0 path.
Signed A/B updates with rollback.
Docs, SBOM, checksums and release notes.
nodes.deps: M1–M4; the native tracks; the hardware lab.
nodes.risks: Real-Indy hardware; cloud capacity; last-mile compatibility.
nodes.note: v1.0 is not dated; the native v0.1.3 image remains the last shipped release.

nodes.title: L2 migration
nodes.summary: Arbitrary-safepoint migration is v2; v1 migrates L0 at message boundaries.
nodes.reason: The v1 contract is L0; L2 needs a different runtime and a much larger test surface.

nodes.title: Home groups
nodes.summary: Multi-object home groups are v2.
nodes.reason: v1 keeps one home per object; groups complicate leases and re-homing.

nodes.title: Multi-object transactions
nodes.summary: Cross-object atomic transactions are v2.
nodes.reason: Per-object linearisability is the v1 promise.

nodes.title: COSMIC on Indy
nodes.summary: The Indy gets an IRIX-inspired native desktop, not a Wayland/GPU stack.
nodes.reason: No Wayland, DRM or GBM on the Indy native path; COSMIC is the GPU-node path.

nodes.title: Vendor GPU stack
nodes.summary: GPU access is an object path, not a local vendor driver.
nodes.reason: The Indy submits command buffers to a GPU object; there is no fake local-bus coherency.

nodes.title: XFS writes
nodes.summary: XFS is read-only; log replay and write-back are out.
nodes.reason: A read-only compatibility server is the smaller, honest promise.

nodes.title: Indigo Magic parity
nodes.summary: The new desktop is IRIX-inspired, not a pixel-for-pixel recreation.
nodes.reason: The goal is a good native desktop, not a museum exhibit.

nodes.title: Forward compatibility
nodes.summary: Native IRIX 7 binaries will not run on IRIX 6.5.
nodes.reason: Backward compatibility is the mandate; forward compatibility is explicitly out.

nodes.title: I7FS
nodes.summary: CAS is the primary mutable-object store; no new on-disk format in v1.
nodes.reason: The namespace is a tree of canonical directory objects over CAS; I7FS is a later experiment.
